patch_description: Replace the current two-parameter (theta, phi) design with a single-parameter "theta" ansatz that stacks two tri-axis rotation + dense-CZ (ring + antipodal) sub-blocks back-to-back inside one ansatz-block definition. This mirrors the best-performing prior seed (single shared theta driving RX/RY/RZ layers with a ring+antipodal CZ entangler, which achieved score 0.80 and fast convergence at 60 steps) but doubles the internal depth by repeating the rotate-entangle-rotate pattern twice, still reusing the same single trainable "theta" parameter throughout. The intuition (from the recommendation) is that adding a second moderate-depth block with extreme parameter sharing increases expressivity/entangling power without adding any new trainable parameters, which should preserve or improve accuracy/generalization while further reducing the number of optimization steps needed to converge, at zero extra parameter cost. This also eliminates the second "phi" parameter entirely, restoring parameter economy (1 unique parameter per block instead of 2), which should raise parameter_efficiency substantially compared to the current 0.72-score, 14-parameter candidate.
